To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can learn a perception model that improves object detection performance in novel environments by just moving around and observing objects in these environments, and that we can use the improved perception to learn a better exploration policy for Object Goal Navigation.

(1) We propose a self-supervised framework for active learning that uses a perception model trained on internet images. It learns to explore the environment to gather observations that can be used to train the perception model.

We propose a framework called Self- supervised Embodied Active Learning that utilizes internet images to learn both action (exploration policy) and perception (semantic maps) in a completely self- supervised manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to leverage the data of Internet images to improve perception and active exploration in embodied agents.
the question of how we can use the vast amount of data and models of the Internet for robot perception and action.
how we can build a self-supervised active learning system that learns from the internet and adapts to robot vision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown that the SEAL framework is capable of closing the action-perception-loop and improving object detection and instance segmenation in a self-supervised manner without requiring any additional labels.
SEAL is an efficient and effective method for self-supervised active learning in robotics.
the SEAL framework enables a robot to improve its vision by exploring the world, without requiring any human labels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how we can use internet images to learn a self-supervised exploration policy that can be used to collect data to improve perception and the improved perception can be used to learn a navigation policy.
SEAL can be used to bootstrap an agent to learn both action-perception in a completely self supervised manner and can be used to transfer the agent to a new environment.
we show how we can build a perception system that can be trained on Internet images and used in real world environments with no labels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet can be used to bootstrap the perception and exploration of robots in the real world.
